newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa closes weaker, pressured by hedge sale.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa closes weaker, pressured by hedge sale.

text.p: Cocoa futures held above earlier lows in light trading at the start of the week but values remained rangebound amid a lack of stimulus from the New York market, traders said on Monday.

Hedge sales from Far Easter operators pressured values earlier in the session, with the bulk of the thin turnover deriving from against actuals trades posted against spot March ahead of first notice day.
"With New York closed, it's not really helping. It's a very quiet in general terms...but the market is making some attempt to consolidate," said one trader.
The New York market is closed for President's Day.
Market sources said the latest CFTC Commitment of Traders report had been partly to blame for the selling. Some traders called the data "disappointing".
The report released late on Friday showed a net speculative short position of just under 2,500 lots.
"People were thinking that it would be nearer to 5,000/10,000," one said.
At the close March stood three stg lower at 849 stg and May was up one at 876 stg. Other positions were unchanged to slightly lower after a day of tight ranges.
In fundamental news, Ghana cocoa purchases to the end of the 15th week of the 1996/97 season, ending January 23, were a cumulative 260,506 tonnes.
This compared with 303,867 tonnes at the end of the 16th week of the year-earlier season, which ended on January 25, 1996.
